title: Probe HTTP Error Hotspots
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=uptime:probe
| stats count as checks, sum(eval(status_code>=500)) as server_errors by service
| eval error_pct=round(100*server_errors/checks,1)
| where checks>=10 AND error_pct>5
| sort - error_pct
description: Highlights services that are technically up but returning too many server errors, the awkward middle ground between green and genuinely healthy.
value: Uptime alone misses a lot of user pain; an HTTP error-rate view catches the endpoints that are alive enough to answer and broken enough to matter.
implementation: Forward probe status codes to Splunk; review services with elevated 5xx rates and pair the findings with application logs.
visualization: Table of services by probe count and HTTP error percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It records which self-hosted apps are answering requests but still failing often enough that users would notice.
